stories.title: Jio Platforms' grey market premium jumps to Rs 218 ahead of October 21 launch; price band set at Rs 1,065-1,119
stories.dek: Jio Platforms is experiencing a rise in grey market premium ahead of its initial public offering. The IPO is set to open on October 21 and will close on October 23. Reliance Industries has established a price band between ₹1,065 and ₹1,119 for the shares.

stories.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms children
stories.dek: The lawsuits, which were filed in state courts, are seeking an order forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works for children. The states are also seeking an order forcing the company to give up profits it has generated from young users.

stories.title: Canada sees scope for more investments in India after Fairfax-IDBI bank deal, says Minister Sidhu
stories.dek: Canada's Minister of International Trade has noted the investment potential between Canada and India in infrastructure development. Following IDBI Bank's sale, Canadian companies aim to expand their presence in key sectors.

stories.dek: Jio Platforms has set its IPO price band at ₹1,065- ₹1,119 per share. At the upper end, the offering could raise about ₹30,213 crore, potentially making it India's largest IPO. Eligible employees will receive a ₹54-per-share discount.

stories.title: Jio Platforms IPO to raise $3.2bn, opens 21 Oct
stories.dek: While the company has not cut the number of shares on offer, with the IPO still comprising of 270 million new shares, the offer is now valued at around ₹30,200 crore, or about $3.2 billion, at the upper end of the ₹1,069-1,119 price per share.

Jio IPO to open on October 21: 10 things to know about the Rs 30,000 crore mega issue
stories.dek: Jio Platforms will open its Rs 30,000 crore IPO for subscription on October 21, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for October 19. The issue could become India's largest-ever public offering, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's record IPO.

stories.title: Centre set to cross Rs 80000 cr disinvestment target for first time since FY19 after IDBI Bank stake sale
stories.dek: The Indian government is expected to surpass its budgeted disinvestment target of Rs 80,000 crore for FY27. A significant contributor will be the strategic sale of IDBI Bank, which is valued at over Rs 52,878 crore.
